pharm: Multimodal serotonergic antidepressant that inhibits the serotonin transporter and directly modulates several 5-HT receptors (5-HT3, 5-HT7, 5-HT1D antagonist; 5-HT1B partial agonist; 5-HT1A agonist), enhancing central serotonergic neurotransmission.
quick: Start 10 mg once daily; increase to 20 mg/day as tolerated; 5 mg if not tolerated
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; possible neonatal symptoms in third trimester
Limited data; weigh benefit; monitor infant
No adjustment for mild-moderate; not studied in severe impairment
summary: Vortioxetine is a multimodal serotonergic antidepressant approved for major depressive disorder in adults. It carries the antidepressant class boxed warning for increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients. It is contraindicated with MAOIs, can cause serotonin syndrome, hyponatremia and increased bleeding, and the dose is halved in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers.
indications: Not approved for use in pediatric patients

dosage.n: For patients not tolerating higher doses

dosage.d: Reduce 15 or 20 mg/day to 10 mg/day for 1 week before stopping
dosage.n: May be stopped abruptly if needed

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Screen for bipolar disorder before starting
Reduce dose by half with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors; cap at 10 mg/day in known CYP2D6 poor metabolizers
Consider a dose increase (not exceeding 3 times the original) with prolonged strong CYP inducers
Do not start within 14 days of an MAOI; wait 21 days after stopping vortioxetine before an MAOI
Reduce 15/20 mg doses to 10 mg for a week before discontinuing if feasible
moa: Vortioxetine's antidepressant effect is thought to result from enhancement of central serotonergic activity. It is a potent, selective inhibitor of the serotonin transporter and also acts directly on serotonin receptors: antagonist at 5-HT3, 5-HT7 and 5-HT1D, partial agonist at 5-HT1B, and agonist at 5-HT1A. The relative contribution of each receptor activity to clinical efficacy is not established; activity is due to the parent drug.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to vortioxetine (anaphylaxis, angioedema, urticaria reported)
Concomitant MAOIs intended for psychiatric disorders, or within 21 days of stopping vortioxetine; within 14 days of stopping an MAOI; or with linezolid or IV methylene blue
relative: History of bleeding disorders or concurrent antiplatelet/anticoagulant use

preg: Limited human data. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk, balancing the risks of untreated maternal depression. Neonates exposed in the third trimester may develop poor adaptation symptoms (respiratory distress, feeding difficulty, jitteriness).
lact: There is limited information on vortioxetine in human milk. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside maternal need and any potential adverse effects on the infant; monitor the breastfed infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed in renal impairment (mild to severe), including end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed for mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Vortioxetine has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment and is not recommended in that setting.

major: MAOIs including linezolid and IV methylene blue (contraindicated; serotonin syndrome)
Other serotonergic drugs - SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans, tramadol, St. John's wort (serotonin syndrome)
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors - bupropion, fluoxetine, paroxetine, quinidine (reduce vortioxetine dose by half)
moderate: Strong CYP inducers - rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin (may need dose increase if used >14 days)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food has no clinically significant effect.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum sodium where hyponatremia risk exists; monitor for bleeding with anticoagulants.

emergency: Acute angle-closure glaucoma (eye pain, visual loss)

monitoring: Suicidal ideation and clinical worsening, especially early and after dose changes
counsel: Take once daily, with or without food
Nausea is the most common side effect and usually improves over the first couple of weeks
Report new or worsening depression, agitation, or suicidal thoughts immediately
Avoid alcohol; tell your doctor about all medicines, especially other antidepressants and MAOIs
Watch for unusual bleeding or bruising, and for confusion or severe weakness (low sodium)
Seek urgent care for eye pain or sudden vision change
Do not stop suddenly; the dose may be tapered
pk: Antidepressant effect over 1-2 weeks; steady state in ~2 weeks
pearls: Boxed warning: increased suicidal thoughts/behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients - monitor closely
Multimodal mechanism: SERT inhibition plus direct serotonin-receptor modulation
Long ~66-hour half-life means it can be stopped without taper, though tapering higher doses is preferred
Halve the dose with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors and cap at 10 mg in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers
Watch for hyponatremia, serotonin syndrome and bleeding; contraindicated with MAOIs
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: No specific antidote. Ingestions of 40-75 mg increased nausea, dizziness, diarrhea, somnolence and flushing; overdoses above 80 mg have been linked to serotonin syndrome (with another serotonergic drug) and seizure. Provide supportive care and contact a poison control center or toxicologist.
